questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Solve 7^(2x−1)=150 by logarithms, giving x to three decimal places. [4 marks]
questions.modelAnswer: Taking natural logs gives (2x−1)ln7=ln150. Therefore 2x−1=ln150/ln7. Rearrange to x=(1+ln150/ln7)/2. Evaluate x≈1.787.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: An obtuse angle θ satisfies (3sinθ+2cosθ)²+(6sinθ−cosθ)²=25. Find sinθ exactly, explaining the sign. [5 marks]
markPoints: Expand: the cross terms +12sinθcosθ and −12sinθcosθ cancel.
For an obtuse θ sine is positive, so sinθ=√2/2.
questions.modelAnswer: Expand: the cross terms +12sinθcosθ and −12sinθcosθ cancel. So 45sin²θ+5cos²θ=25. Since cos²θ=1−sin²θ, solve 40sin²θ=20. Hence sinθ=±1/√2. For an obtuse θ sine is positive, so sinθ=√2/2.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A saver deposits £120 at the start of each month and earns 0.5% interest at each month-end. Calculate the account balance immediately after interest in month six. Give one model limitation. [5 marks]
markPoints: The first deposit earns interest for six months and the last for one month.
This is geometric with ratio 1.005 and six terms.
The calculation assumes a constant rate and no withdrawals or fees.
questions.modelAnswer: The first deposit earns interest for six months and the last for one month. Balance=120(1.005+1.005²+⋯+1.005⁶). This is geometric with ratio 1.005 and six terms. Use S=120×1.005(1.005⁶−1)/0.005≈£732.71. The calculation assumes a constant rate and no withdrawals or fees.

questions.prompt: A model is y=a+b log₁₀t for t>0. Its graph passes through (1,4) and (100,10). Find a and b, predict y when t=10 and explain why t=0 is invalid. [5 marks]
markPoints: The logarithm of zero is undefined; t must be positive.
questions.modelAnswer: At t=1, log₁₀1=0 so a=4. At t=100, 10=4+2b. Therefore b=3 and y=4+3log₁₀t. At t=10, y=7. The logarithm of zero is undefined; t must be positive.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Find the constant, x and x² terms of the binomial expansion of 1/[(1−2x)(2+x)], and state its common interval of validity. [6 marks]
markPoints: The coefficients of x and x² are respectively 3/4 and 13/8.
questions.modelAnswer: Expand (1−2x)^−1=1+2x+4x²+⋯. Rewrite (2+x)^−1=(1/2)(1+x/2)^−1. Expand as 1/2−x/4+x²/8+⋯. The product has constant term 1/2. The coefficients of x and x² are respectively 3/4 and 13/8. Both series converge for |x|<1/2.

questions.prompt: Show that f(x)=x³−6x²+12x has a stationary point of inflection at x=2 and find its coordinates. [5 marks]
markPoints: Hence f′(2)=0 and the tangent is stationary.
Since f″ changes from negative to positive across 2 there is an inflection.
questions.modelAnswer: Differentiate f′(x)=3(x−2)². Hence f′(2)=0 and the tangent is stationary. Differentiate f″(x)=6x−12. Since f″ changes from negative to positive across 2 there is an inflection. f(2)=8, so the point is (2,8).

questions.prompt: Prove that the open real interval 1<x<2 has no smallest member. [4 marks]
markPoints: Assume that a smallest member x exists with 1<x<2.
This contradicts x being the least member, so no least member exists.
questions.modelAnswer: Assume that a smallest member x exists with 1<x<2. Set y=(1+x)/2. Then 1<y<x<2. This contradicts x being the least member, so no least member exists.

questions.prompt: Between x=a and x=b a curve encloses 36 square units above and 11 below the x-axis. Find its definite integral and its total enclosed area. [3 marks]
markPoints: Area above the axis contributes positively.

questions.prompt: Temperature follows T=90−70e^(−kt), where t≥0, k>0 and T=55 at t=2. Find k, the time to reach T=81 and the limiting temperature. [5 marks]
markPoints: As t tends to infinity T approaches 90.
questions.modelAnswer: At t=2, e^(−2k)=1/2. Hence k=(ln2)/2. For T=81, e^(−kt)=9/70. Therefore t=2ln(70/9)/ln2≈5.919. As t tends to infinity T approaches 90.

questions.prompt: Prove from first principles that f′(x)=4x−3 for f(x)=2x²−3x. [5 marks]
markPoints: After subtracting f(x), the numerator is 4xh+2h²−3h.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Evaluate exactly the definite integral of x ln x between 1 and e. [5 marks]
markPoints: Use integration by parts with u=ln x, dv=x dx.
The result at e minus at 1 is (e²+1)/4.
questions.modelAnswer: Use integration by parts with u=ln x, dv=x dx. Then du=(1/x)dx and v=x²/2. An antiderivative is (x²/2)ln x−∫x/2 dx. Simplify to (x²/2)ln x−x²/4. The result at e minus at 1 is (e²+1)/4.
